{{Short description|none}}
The [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série A]] is the professional [[association football]] league of [[Brazil]]. This is a '''list of Brasileirão Série A winning football managers'''. Including since 1959, after the unification of the champions of the Torneio Roberto Gomes Pedrosa and [[Taça Brasil]].

The record for most titles is shared by two managers who won five each. [[Luis Alonso Perez|Lula]] won five consecutively for [[Santos FC|Santos]] from [[1961 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|1961]] to [[1965 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|1965]]. [[Vanderlei Luxemburgo]] won five with [[Palmeiras]] ([[1993 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|1993]], [[1994 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|1994]]), [[Sport Club Corinthians Paulista|Corinthians]] ([[1998 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|1998]]), [[Cruzeiro Esporte Clube|Cruzeiro]] ([[2003 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|2003]]) and Santos ([[2004 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|2004]]).

Three foreigners have won the title: Argentine [[Carlos Volante]] for [[EC Bahia|Bahia]] in the debut season in [[1959 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|1959]],<ref>{{cite news |last1=Signor |first1=Luiz |title=Jesus só precisa de 25 jogos para repetir argentino e fazer história|trans-title=Jesus only needed 25 games to repeat Argentine and make history |url=https://br.onefootball.com/jesus-so-precisa-de-25-jogos-para-repetir-argentino-e-fazer-historia/ |accessdate=27 November 2019 |publisher=One Football |date=25 November 2019 |language=Portuguese}}</ref> Portuguese [[Jorge Jesus]] for [[Flamengo]] in [[2019 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|2019]] and [[Abel Ferreira]] for [[SE Palmeiras|Palmeiras]] in [[2022 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|2022]].

==Seasons and winning managers==
[[File:Lula - A 1962.jpg|thumb|upright|[[Luís Alonso Pérez|Lula]] won five Campeonatos Brasileiro titles in a row as Santos manager in the 1960s.]]
[[Image:Wanderley Luxemburgo 2010.jpg|thumb|upright|[[Vanderlei Luxemburgo]] was the winning manager five times, with Palmeiras (1993, 1994), Corinthians (1998), Cruzeiro (2003) and Santos (2004).]]
[[File:Carlos_Volante.jpg|thumb|upright|Argentine manager [[Carlos Volante]] won the first title in 1959 for Bahia.]]
[[File:Jorge_Jesus_2012.jpg|thumb|upright|[[Jorge Jesus]] from Portugal won with Flamengo in 2019, becoming the first foreign manager to win since Volante.]]
